summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, morbid obesity, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement was readmitted for worsening left leg pain, redness, and serous drainage three days after completing oral linezolid. She had no fever or systemic signs of infection. Physical exam showed circumferential redness and shallow ulceration with clear drainage, concerning for recurrent cellulitis or worsening stasis dermatitis. Given lack of improvement on linezolid, she was restarted on IV vancomycin via a newly placed PICC line with renal dose adjustment. A left leg ultrasound ruled out DVT. Her heart failure remained stable on home diuretics, and anticoagulation with warfarin was continued with INR monitoring. She improved clinically, was discharged home with home health for IV antibiotics and wound care, and instructed to continue compression, elevation, and topical steroid for her leg.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Heart valve replaced by other means
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
